text: Newcastle disease is one of the most common and economically damaging diseases in Cambodian backyard poultry flocks, causing sudden high mortality, respiratory distress, and greenish diarrhea. Regular vaccination on a fixed schedule (commonly using thermostable I-2 strain vaccine, suited to village conditions without a strong cold chain) is the most effective prevention. Sick birds should be isolated immediately and not sold or slaughtered for consumption, since this can spread the disease to other flocks in the village. Village animal health workers or the provincial Office of Animal Health and Production can provide vaccination and diagnosis support.
